name: sortstable
algorithm: Each standard library's stable sort of n (key, id) records of two u32, key splitmix64 % 1000 and id the index, by key: per round r the keys come from seed + r * 0x5555555555555555; every 1,024th id times its index plus the last record is added to the checksum with wrapping (README.md). Equal keys keep id order, so the result is unique.

skip.c: no stable sort in C's standard library
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; a stable order is unique, so the sampled ids check every column
notes: Algorithms and memory: Mk Slice.SortStable is Go's stable_func (insertion sort of 20-element blocks, then SymMerge; in place, no allocation, O(n log^2 n) moves); Go slices.SortStableFunc is the same algorithm; Zig std.mem.sort is an in-place block sort (WikiSort), O(n log n); Rust slice::sort_by_key is driftsort, which allocates a scratch buffer of up to n elements.
